title: The relayer's own minimum-output argument must itself clear a floor derived from pool rates and governance slippage
content:
Curve and Uniswap both accept a caller-supplied minimum output, which on its own is only as strong as the caller's diligence. A...8.1.4 removes that discretion:

```
uint256 minimumMinAmountOut = params.amountIn * rates[params.inputIndex] * params.maxSlippage
    / rates[params.outputIndex] / 1e18;
require(params.minAmountOut >= minimumMinAmountOut, "CurveLib/min-amount-not-met");
```

The check is a **constraint on the constraint**. The relayer still chooses `minAmountOut`, but may only choose a value at least as protective as the one implied by the pool's `stored_rates` and the governance-set `maxSlippage`. Passing `1` — the classic way to accidentally or deliberately accept any execution price — reverts.

The same shape appears twice more with different reference prices: A...8.2.4 requires `minLpAmount` to clear `valueDeposited * maxSlippage / get_virtual_price()`, and A...8.3.4 requires the aggregated `minWithdrawAmounts` to clear `lpBurnAmount * get_virtual_price() * maxSlippage / 1e36`. In all three the pool's own accounting rate supplies the fair-value estimate and governance supplies the tolerance.

This is what lets Grove delegate execution to a relayer without trusting the relayer's price judgment: the worst execution the relayer can authorise is bounded by parameters the relayer does not control.
description: Curve requires minAmountOut to be at least amountIn scaled by stored_rates and maxSlippage, so a caller cannot disarm slippage protection simply by passing a trivially low minimum.
